reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence, and the key premises—especially the persistence of graphite or MoS2 lubricating films up to 800 °C in a CoCrFeNi matrix—are specific claims requiring experimental support that is not provided.
premises: Solid lubricants like graphite or MoS2 form low-shear-strength films at sliding interfaces
Such lubricating films can persist and remain effective from room temperature up to 800 °C
Adding solid lubricant to a CoCrFeNi matrix will reduce friction and wear compared to the unreinforced alloy
